Predict growth and mortality for individual observed trees

Source: R/finn-class.R
predictTrees.Rd

Predict growth and mortality for individual observed trees

Usage

predictTrees(
  model,
  tree_data,
  env,
  patches = 100L,
  patch_size = NULL,
  device = c("cpu", "gpu")
)

Arguments

model

(finn_class)
A (fitted) model.

tree_data

(data.table|data.frame)
Observed trees: siteID, year, patchID, species, dbh (at the interval start) and period_length (the interval, in timesteps).

env

(data.table|data.frame)
Environment, as for fit.

patches

(integer(1))
Not used: the patch dimension of the observed-tree tensors is the number of distinct patchIDs in tree_data (it used to be patches, and the extra patches were empty). Kept so existing calls run unchanged.

patch_size

(numeric(1))
Area of one patch in ha. Defaults to the one the model was last fitted or simulated with (model$patch_size_ha); pass a value only to override it. A model that was never fitted or simulated has none, so give it here. The value is stored on the model.

device

(character(1))
"cpu" or "gpu"; "cuda" is accepted as a synonym for "gpu".

Value

One row per row of tree_data, in the same order (.row records the original position), with growth_pred (the relative growth rate per year over the interval, compounded as described above) and mort_pred (probability of dying during the interval). Bind these onto tree_data directly rather than joining on siteID/year/patchID, which would be many-to-many.

Details

The tree-level counterpart of predict.finn_class. Where predict() simulates a stand forward and reports site-level states, this evaluates the growth and mortality kernels on trees you observed: light is computed from the observed stand, the kernels run on those trees at their observed diameters, and the annual rates are accumulated over each site's remeasurement interval — growth as the per-year rate of the compounded annual rates (the geometric mean of 1 + g, as makeObsData() derives the observed rate), mortality as the complement of the product of annual survivals.

It is the same code path fit(..., loss_aggregation = c(growth = "tree", mortality = "tree")) scores, so a validation report cannot drift from the objective it is validating.

See also

predict.finn_class() / simulateForest() for the simulated stand, finn_loss for the per-tree losses that share this code, fia_tree_dt for a table of observed trees with their fates

Examples

library(data.table)
# the growth and mortality kernels applied to the trees as observed, so the
# error of the two functions alone, with no simulated stand in between
sites <- 1:3
Nsp   <- max(fia_obs_dt$species)
init  <- makeInitCohorts(fia_init_trees[siteID %in% sites], Nspecies = Nsp)
FINN.seed(1)
m <- finn(
  N_species            = Nsp, recruits_dbh = 12.9,
  growth_process       = createProcess(~ temp + prec, FINN::growth),
  mortality_process    = createProcess(~ temp + prec, FINN::mortality),
  regeneration_process = createProcess(~ temp + prec, FINN::regeneration))
fit(m, data = fia_obs_dt[siteID %in% sites], env = fia_env_dt[siteID %in% sites],
    init_cohort = init, epochs = 2L, patches = 4, patch_size = 0.06,
    plot_progress = FALSE)
#> ℹ weights: intercept-only baseline x your vector (dbh=0.00243, ba=12, trees=0.968, growth=1.84e+04, mortality=38.5, regeneration=0.768)
#> ℹ share of the objective at the intercept-only baseline (scaled): dbh=17%, ba=17%, trees=17%, growth=17%, mortality=17%, regeneration=17%

# `fia_init_trees` is a pure initial state, so name the census the trees are
# scored against and the interval, in timesteps (years), that reaches it
trees <- fia_init_trees[siteID %in% sites,
                        .(siteID, patchID, species, dbh, year = 10L,
                          period_length = 10)]
pred  <- predictTrees(m, tree_data = trees,
                      env = fia_env_dt[siteID %in% sites], patch_size = 0.06)
#> [tree_data] 87 trees, up to 16 per patch and observation year
head(pred)
#>     .row siteID  year patchID growth_pred mort_pred
#>    <int>  <int> <int>   <int>       <num>     <num>
#> 1:     1      1    10       1 0.006177030 0.1652927
#> 2:     2      1    10       1 0.000000000 0.1834491
#> 3:     3      1    10       1 0.001696481 0.1784589
#> 4:     4      1    10       1 0.007360663 0.1722142
#> 5:     5      1    10       1 0.000000000 0.1835063
#> 6:     6      1    10       2 0.016580803 0.1630244

# the bundled tree table carries the observed fates, so prediction and
# observation can be compared tree by tree: here the predicted probability
# of dying within the interval for the trees that died and those that lived
obs_trees <- fia_tree_dt[siteID %in% sites]
p <- predictTrees(m, tree_data = obs_trees, env = fia_env_dt[siteID %in% sites],
                  patch_size = 0.06)
#> [tree_data] 113 trees, up to 14 per patch and observation year
tapply(p$mort_pred, obs_trees$died, mean)
#>         0         1 
#> 0.1686863 0.1718107
